issues.title: Folding a split review keeps only part 1's usage record, so parts 2..N spend is lost.
issues.why: Each part now stamps its own USAGE_KEY record in _run_part, but review_fold._metadata copies parts[0].metadata and only sums TOOL_CALLS_MADE_KEY. The folded step result persisted to run state therefore carries part 1's tokens/turns/cost only, and pipeline review artifacts are excluded from sq stats reviews, so the rest of the spend appears nowhere. This undercounts exactly what slice 175 exists to measure.

issues.title: A provider failure in one part of a split review no longer stops the loop and makes the fold raise TypeError, hiding the provider error.
issues.why: The ProviderError branch of _run_part used to re-raise; it now returns _exception_result with outputs={} and verdict None. _review's loop has no early exit, so later parts still make paid model calls, then fold_review_parts calls _part_input which raises TypeError('review part must name exactly one input file, got []'). execute's catch-all reports that TypeError as the step error, dropping the provider message and the per-part usage records.

issues.title: The existing two-part provider-failure test passes on the TypeError because it never checks result.error or call count.
issues.why: test_provider_failure_on_part_two_keeps_part_one asserts only success is False, artifacts and a log line, so it is green despite the bug in 175-I2. The claim is true, but it is a test-strength point; the defect itself is graded in I2.

issues.title: A failed SDK compact drops the spend carried on the ProviderError or captured before a reconnect failure.
issues.why: SDKExecutionSession.dispatch now attaches telemetry to a ProviderError, and compact() captures the summary reply before _reconnect; but CompactAction's except branch returns a failed ActionResult with no metadata, and a reconnect failure discards reply.telemetry. Dispatch, summary and review all stamp failed-call usage per D5, and success criterion 2 names failed compact actions. The row shows as unrecorded rather than silently, but the spend is lost.

issues.title: Compact usage records are built with resolved=None, so alias is None and subscription costs are labeled as provider money.
issues.why: compact.py calls record_from_telemetry(None, ...), so _build sets alias=None. cost_cell only labels a provider cost 'api-rate equiv.' when _is_subscription(record.alias) is true, and returns False for None, so every SDK compact row on a subscription alias renders '$X prov', contradicting D3, while dispatch and summary rows for the same alias are labeled correctly. The comment claiming no resolution is needed is wrong for labeling.

issues.title: Findings-addressed judge spend (and prompt-only compact spend) is not recorded and gates are excluded from LLM action counting.
issues.why: True that judge_residue_core's review spend is never stamped and GATE is not in LLM_ACTION_TYPES, but the judge code was not changed in this diff and the slice design explicitly lists the addressed-findings judge as out of scope; compact capture is scoped to the SDK session path. This is a documented scope gap, not a defect in the changed code.

issues.title: Review frontmatter cost key names are spelled separately in the writer and the stats reader.
issues.why: run_cost.py writes the key literals and reviews_report.py repeats them in _INT_KEYS and its _int/_float/_basis calls. It is a DRY point; the keys currently agree, so nothing is wrong at head.

issues.title: The reviews reader tests use hand-written frontmatter instead of the real writer.
issues.why: The fixtures are hand-written. This is a test-coverage concern for an already-working reader, not a defect.

issues.title: Usage-fold and one-shot plumbing logic is duplicated between the SDK agent and the session turns.
issues.why: ClaudeSDKAgent._fold_result and DispatchTurns.fold_result do the same read-warn-fold steps. Duplication is a maintainability point with no wrong behavior at head.

issues.title: dispatch.py, _execute_summary and _dispatch_via_session exceed the length guidelines.
issues.why: File and function length are style guideline points; the lengths largely predate the diff and cause no defect.

issues.title: SDK prompt token total is a partial sum when a cache field is malformed.
issues.why: read_result_usage adds only the cache classes that parse, so a malformed cache value gives prompt equal to the uncached count; the code matches its docstring and logs a WARNING. Real SDK results carry both keys as ints, so this is hardening against input that does not arrive.

issues.title: get_all_aliases re-parses models.toml on each call and the diff adds calls on async paths.
issues.why: resolver._resolved now calls get_all_aliases per resolve, adding to several existing calls. An unmeasured performance point with no shown effect.

issues.title: review_client prices with a fresh warned set, bypassing the per-run pricing-warning dedup.
issues.why: resolve_cost(..., set()) at review_client lines 315 and 321 means a partially priced alias warns once per review instead of once per run. True, but the only effect is repeated WARNING lines; costs are correct.

issues.title: record_from_error re-resolves a failed review's cost instead of reusing exc.cost_usd/cost_basis.
issues.why: review_client resolves cost onto the exception, then UsageCapture.record_from_error calls _build which resolves again from the same telemetry and the same alias (settings.resolved.alias is passed to both), so the values agree. The effect is duplicated pricing logic and a possible second warning, not wrong data.

issues.title: The subscription cost-tier literal is defined again in stats_views rather than once.
issues.why: SUBSCRIPTION_TIER='subscription' duplicates a value used in other modules. Style/DRY rule point; behavior is correct.

issues.title: An unreadable or non-UTF-8 review artifact aborts sq stats reviews instead of being skipped.
issues.why: read_frontmatter calls path.read_text without catching OSError/UnicodeDecodeError, and reviews_usage_report does not catch them. True, but artifacts are written by squadron as UTF-8, so this is hardening against input that does not normally arrive.

issues.title: A list or mapping costBasis value raises TypeError (unhashable) in the reviews report.
issues.why: _basis tests value in a set, which raises TypeError for an unhashable YAML value. True, but squadron writes costBasis as a scalar string, so only a hand-corrupted artifact triggers it.

issues.title: effort_for_session is annotated -> None yet its result is used as the effort value.
issues.why: The function always returns None and callers bind it to effort_sent, which is the intended D7 value today. Naming/clarity point with no wrong behavior.

issues.title: sq stats run omits earlier loop rounds because only the final round's action_results are persisted.
issues.why: Loop steps keep earlier rounds in StepResult.prior_rounds, but StateManager._append_step serializes only step_result.action_results and RunStateRecorder.round_completed records nothing. The new run_usage_report reads only persisted action_results, so a multi-round loop reports only its last round, contradicting the slice's stated 'the cost of a loop is the whole loop' and 'run totals include failed attempts'.

issues.title: Fan-out branch usage records are discarded by the fan-in reducers and on branch failure.
issues.why: The diff passes usage_capture into fan-out branches, but CollectReducer and FirstPassReducer build a new ActionResult without metadata, and the failed-branch path returns action_results=[]. The persisted action has type 'fan_out', which is not in LLM_ACTION_TYPES, so the lost spend is not even counted as unrecorded.

issues.title: The review ProviderError branch logs a misleading 'unexpected error' with a traceback after its WARNING.
issues.why: The new branch calls _logger.exception('review: unexpected error ...'). Before the diff the re-raise reached execute's catch-all, which logged the same message with a traceback, so log output is unchanged; the wording is merely inaccurate and inconsistent with dispatch.

issues.title: effort_sent_by_profile inside the except block could raise and mask the original ProviderError.
issues.why: effort_sent_by_profile calls get_profile, ensure_provider_loaded and get_provider for the same profile run_review_with_profile has already looked up and loaded, so those calls cannot realistically fail at that point. Speculative hardening.

issues.title: sq stats reviews --json prints plain text when the review directory is missing.
issues.why: The missing_dir check runs before the as_json branch, so --json outputs 'No review directory at ...' with exit 0. True, but the only shipped consumers (the sq-stats skill and slash command) display output rather than parse it, and the case is a project with no reviews directory.

issues.title: Moving the dispatch except ProviderError clause above other handlers could misroute subclasses.
issues.why: None of the later-handled types subclass ProviderError: ModelResolutionError and ModelPoolNotImplemented subclass Exception, ContextForgeError subclasses Exception, ProjectRulesError subclasses RuntimeError, and KeyError is builtin. The reordering changes no matching.

issues.title: run_usage_report catches AttributeError and re-declares STATE_READ_ERRORS.
issues.why: The except tuple is broader than STATE_READ_ERRORS and includes AttributeError, which could relabel a bug as an unreadable file. A maintainability point; no wrong behavior shown.
